subject: Re: Pilot pricing — minimums, bundling and concession matrix
message_1_subject: Pilot pricing questions: minimums and bundle structure
message_1_body:
Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency profile looks promising. Before we lock the pilot, procurement asked for clarification on three items related to billing: token minimums, how you bucket long-context calls (we have a lot of 8k+ prompts), and rounding behavior for streaming responses. Specifically:

- Do you enforce a minimum token floor per call, per session, or per invoice period for hosted customers?
- For prompts that exceed a single context window, is there an automatic split (and how are the pieces billed)?
- If we stream responses and they stop early, are we charged on the final token count or rounded up to a quantum?

We'd also like to understand what concessions look like for a three-month pilot (100k tokens/day average, occasional 50k spikes). Can you send a short concession matrix and an SOW draft we can review with legal?

Best,
Elaine
Elaine Park
Head of AI Platforms, FinLytics
[attachment: sample_usage.csv (csv)]
message_2_subject: Re: Pilot pricing questions: minimums and bundle structure
message_2_body:
Hi Elaine — thanks, great questions. I'll summarize our standard behavior and then propose a pilot concession matrix. Short answers up front:

- Minimums: we don't bill per-call minimums for hosted customers; instead we apply an invoice-period minimum (monthly minimum in the contract). For pilots we can set a shorter commit with a reduced floor.
- Long-context: our billing splits are based on configured context buckets. If a request exceeds a single context variant, we charge for each context slice used; we try to merge contiguous KV cache use to avoid double-charging.
- Streaming rounding: we bill on tokens emitted; streaming truncation is measured on actual tokens delivered but then rounded up to the nearest billing quantum (default quantum = 8 tokens).

I'll put together a 3-tier concession matrix and a SOW draft and loop Camila for the formal numbers and Grace for legal/ops review. Expect those within two business days.

Cheers,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[phone redacted]
message_3_subject: Concession matrix draft for FinLytics pilot
message_3_body:
Karthik / Grace,

Draft concession matrix below (numbers for discussion):

Tier A (Pilot baseline) — 3 months
- Commitment: 100k tokens/day average (monthly true-up)
- Invoice-period minimum: 40% of committed avg per month (pilot discount)
- Discount: 20% off list token price
- Context handling: up to 32k context windows included; >32k billed as additional slices at 0.6x token rate
- Rounding quantum: 8 tokens (default)

Tier B (Pilot + burst protection) 
- Commitment: same as Tier A + 50% burst reserve
- Invoice-period minimum: 60%
- Discount: 25%
- Context handling: up to 48k included; automatic reassembly credit for repeated KV reuse

Tier C (Pilot with committed seat + support)
- Commitment: 120k tokens/day + 2 dedicated seats
- Invoice-period minimum: 80%
- Discount: 30%
- Context handling: up to 64k; 1 free large-slice conversion per 10k requests

Notes: all pilots include a one-time SOW fee; rounding/quantum can be softened to 1 token quantum for high-volume calls as a concession but requires a committed telemetry hook to prove usage pattern (we need to enable high-precision metering).

Attaching a redlined pricing PDF and SOW template for FinLytics. Please review and I can turn into a DocuSign-ready SOW.

Camila
Sr. Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

message_4_subject: Re: Concession matrix draft for FinLytics pilot
message_4_body:
Camila — thanks, this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from procurement and legal:

1) Invoice-period minimum: procurement wants the minimum as an absolute monthly floor (tokens), not a percent. Can you provide the concrete token counts per month for each tier?
2) Long-context billing: clarify "slice" size and show two worked examples (one 80k prompt split across 3 slices; one 150k content ingest where KV reuse applies).
3) Rounding quantum: we'd like the pilot to use 1-token quantum for a trial period instead of 8. You mentioned a telemetry hook — what data points do you need?

If you can add worked examples and exact per-month minima we can move to redlines next week.

Best,
Elaine
Elaine Park
Head of AI Platforms, FinLytics
[signature omitted]
message_5_subject: Re: Concession matrix draft — worked examples & minima
message_5_body:
Hi Elaine — attached is an updated pricing PDF with the concrete monthly minima and two worked examples (see pages 2-3). Quick summary here: 

- Tier A monthly minima (tokens): 3,000,000 tokens/month (equivalent to 100k/day avg)
- Tier B monthly minima: 4,500,000 tokens/month
- Tier C monthly minima: 5,000,000 tokens/month

Worked examples (excerpt):
- 80k request split: with our 32k slice config that becomes: 32k + 32k + 16k => billed as 3 slices; final slice rounded to slice quantum (8-token quantum) then applied token discounts. If using 1-token quantum concession, the final slice is billed exactly at 16k.
- 150k ingest with KV reuse: initial ingest charged for 5 slices; subsequent calls that hit the same KV prefix only bill delta tokens (example math in PDF).

Telemetry hook: we need a minimal trace: request_id, timestamp, effective_context_size, tokens_in, tokens_out, and a KV_hit boolean. That lets finance validate high-precision metering; we'll only use it for billing reconciliation during the pilot and delete after.

I've attached the updated PDF and a DocuSign-ready SOW link. Let me know if procurement wants the minima expressed as spend equivalents and we'll include sample invoice lines.

Camila
[attachment: FinLytics_Redwood_Pricing_Concessions_v3.pdf (updated)]
message_6_subject: Re: Concession matrix draft — finalize SOW and telemetry
message_6_body:
Hi Elaine — following internal legal review, the proposed minima and telemetry hook look acceptable for a time-limited pilot. Final notes: 

- We will set the pilot telemetry retention to 90 days and provide a deletion affidavit at pilot close.
- We'll set the quantum to 1 token for pilot billing reconciliation only; long-term defaults will revert to 8 tokens unless otherwise negotiated.
- Attached is the SOW (DocuSign link included) with the per-month token minima spelled out and an acceptance clause for the telemetry hook.

Next steps: If FinLytics signs the SOW, finance will issue a pro forma invoice for the first month at the Tier A minima; procurement typically returns redlines within 3 business days.
